From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **We should not accept this.**

- The labels are the Seller's own characterisation in its own draft. Nearly every clause carrying the label is a Seller-favourable position, including several that are plainly not market.
- I have no record of Buyer agreement to any of these. **Please confirm with the deal team** whether anything was agreed in a term sheet or in correspondence I haven't seen. Unless it was, every clause below is open.
- In our response, expressly state that the Buyer does not accept the categorisation and that all positions remain subject to mark-up. That avoids any later argument about a course of dealing or estoppel.

I have reviewed everything on its merits, regardless of labels.

---

## Part A: Limitation and risk-allocation package

### 1. Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties treated as general warranties
**Seller position:** Title and capacity warranties are subject to the 20% cap and 18-month time limit "for administrative simplicity."

**Why it matters:** This is the most significant departure from market. If title is defective, we have paid AUD 24m for shares the Seller could not deliver, but recovery would be capped at AUD 4.8m and lost after 18 months. Title DD rests only on the Seller's own share register (DD-012; see item 14).

**Push back:**
- Title, capacity, authority, solvency and share capital warranties are Fundamental Warranties.
- Cap them at 100% of the purchase price (plus any purchase price adjustments).
- Set the claims period at a minimum of 6–7 years, or the statutory limitation period.
- Exclude them from the de minimis and basket.

### 2. Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 and 12.3/13)
**Seller position:** The limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims. Any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."

**Why it matters:** As drafted, this would sweep in fraud, wilful concealment, specific indemnities, the tax indemnity, leakage and covenant breaches. The default rule is also backwards: it puts the drafting burden on us to carve out each protection.

**Push back:**
- Reverse the default. Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.
- Carve out completely, with no cap, threshold or time limit:
  - fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct and wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers or advisers;
  - Fundamental Warranties (see item 1);
  - specific indemnities and the tax indemnity (separate caps and periods, negotiated individually);
  - leakage and purchase price adjustment claims;
  - breach of pre-Completion covenants.
- **Non-reliance (cl 20.5):** Under NSW law, s18 of the Australian Consumer Law cannot be contracted out of. A non-reliance clause is only evidence on reliance. Even so, we should confirm that it does not apply to fraud, to statements in the Disclosure Letter, or to the Warranties themselves. The Warranties must remain expressly relied upon.

### 3. Thresholds (cl 12.2)
**Seller position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis. AUD 250,000 basket (about 1.04% of price), operating as a deductible: only the excess is recoverable.

**Push back:**
- **Tipping basket:** once the threshold is crossed, recover from the first dollar.
- Reduce the basket to about 0.5% (AUD 120,000) and the de minimis to about AUD 10,000–15,000.
- Aggregate claims arising from the same or related facts for de minimis purposes. Otherwise the Seller can break one problem into sub-threshold pieces.
- No thresholds for Fundamental Warranties, tax or specific indemnities.

### 4. General cap and time limit (cl 12.1 / 12.3)
**Seller position:** 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) and 18 months.

**Assessment:** 20% is within market range but at the Seller-friendly end, given the volume of known risk (items 6–12).

**Push back:**
- A cap of 30% (AUD 7.2m), or keep 20% only if every specific risk below is ring-fenced in specific indemnities with their own caps.
- General claims period of 24 months, covering at least two audit cycles.
- Tax claims period of at least 5–7 years, tied to ATO amendment periods plus a buffer.
- If W&I insurance is in contemplation, recalibrate. It is worth raising now, because it changes the cap dynamics.

### 5. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
**Seller position:** No separate tax or IP protection.

**Push back:**
- A standalone **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax, superannuation guarantee and PAYG on the DD-005 bonuses. It should be dollar-for-dollar, outside the thresholds and subject to its own period.
- **IP warranties** to be strengthened and covered by the Ironquay indemnity (item 9).

---

## Part B: Disclosure and knowledge

### 6. General disclosure of the entire data room and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)
**Why it matters:** Disclosing "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room and public records would hollow out every warranty. The Seller could defeat a claim by pointing to any document anywhere, however obscure.

**Push back:**
- Delete general disclosure of the data room and public registers. At most, accept disclosure of specified documents to the extent fairly disclosed.
- Adopt a **fair disclosure standard**: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed with sufficient detail to allow a reasonable buyer to identify its nature and scope, and against the specific warranty it qualifies.
- Specific disclosures should qualify only the warranties they reference.
- **No updating:** the Disclosure Letter is fixed at signing. Any new matter arising between signing and Completion does not cure breach of repeated warranties. Instead it gives us a termination right or a claim.
- Data room cut-off: 22 September 2026 is six weeks ago. Confirm what has been added since, and that the index is frozen and agreed. Add a USB/archive copy deliverable.

### 7. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)
**Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Why it matters:** This is constructive knowledge, imputed through all our advisers. Combined with item 6, it amounts to near-total exclusion. It would also undermine the specific indemnities: the Seller could argue that because we knew about Ironquay, DD-006 and so on, we cannot claim.

**Push back:**
- Delete it. Our preferred position is an express pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not limit claims.
- **Fallback only:** limit it to the actual knowledge of named individuals of the Buyer (not advisers), of facts they knew constituted a breach, as at signing. Specific indemnities must be expressly excluded from its operation.

### 8. Disclosure Letter non-admission and reservation (1.4, 11)
These are broadly acceptable as boilerplate. We should add that the Disclosure Letter does not:
- extend or create a limitation;
- qualify a Fundamental Warranty, the tax indemnity or any specific indemnity.

---

## Part C: Specific transaction risks (known issues)

These are the substantive problems. Several the Seller itself discloses as unresolved, while simultaneously labelling the related clauses [STANDARD].

### 9. Ironquay IP (DD-004, DD-010; cl 11.1)
**Facts:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

**Why it matters:** Paperbark may not own IP that it is presumably using, and which may be core to the business. An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" covers only the AUD 180,000, not the real exposure: infringement claims, loss of the right to use, rework, injunctions or customer claims.

**Push back:**
- **Condition Precedent:**
  - evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, funded by the Seller or deducted from price; and
  - an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, including moral rights consents.
- Broaden the indemnity to all Losses from any defect in the Company's title to, or right to use, the SOW3 materials or any Ironquay deliverable. It should sit outside the general cap and thresholds, with a cap of at least 100% of price for core IP, or a separately negotiated figure.
- Ask the DD team to establish what SOW3 covers and how central it is to the product.

### 10. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
**Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records are potentially affected (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and notifiability were unknown as at 22 September and the investigation was "preliminary."

**Why it matters:**
- This is potentially an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme. The scheme requires a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within 30 days of the entity becoming aware of reasonable grounds to suspect a breach.
- By today, 5 November, that window may well have expired. If so, there is a risk of OAIC regulatory exposure under the enhanced penalty regime, plus customer notification and contractual consequences. A potential additional issue is that Bluefen or other customers' data may be involved.
- Calling it "not expected to be material" is an assertion with no supporting evidence.

**Push back / actions:**
- **Urgent information request:**
  - the date of awareness;
  - the status of the NDB assessment;
  - whether the OAIC or affected individuals have been notified;
  - whether the link was accessed (access logs) and whether it has been revoked;
  - any forensic report;
  - whose data is in the records, and whether any customer contract notification obligations have been triggered.
- **Pre-Completion covenant:** complete the investigation and any required notifications, with Buyer consultation rights.
- **Specific indemnity** covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party and customer claims. It should sit outside the cap and thresholds, and be unaffected by disclosure or knowledge.
- Consider a **retention/escrow** from the price until the matter is closed out or the limitation risk passes.
- Remove any characterisation of the matter as immaterial from the SPA.

### 11. Riverlark Bank facility (DD-003; cl 2 / 7)
**Facts:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The facility has a change of control clause (8.1) and a discharge clause (9.2). It has not been repaid and no discharge has been obtained.

**Why it matters:** A "release following Completion" is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis. Completion would likely trigger a change of control default under cl 8.1 while the security remains over Company assets that we will then own.

**Push back:**
- The full payout amount, including break costs, accrued interest and fees, is Debt deducted from the price and paid directly to Riverlark from the funds flow at Completion.
- **Completion deliverables:**
  - a payout letter;
  - an executed deed of release;
  - releases of all security interests (PPSR financing change statements), with any mortgage or real property discharges in registrable form.
- No post-Completion release. Add a Seller indemnity for any residual Riverlark liability.

### 12. Bluefen change of control consent (DD-002; cl 3 / 6.3)
**Facts:** Bluefen represents about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m FY26). Consent under cl 11.2 is subject to conditions in cl 11.3. There is no final consent and no evidence the conditions have been satisfied.

**Why it matters:** Losing Bluefen would materially impair the value we are paying AUD 24m for. "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation. Treating the CP as satisfied "on delivery of written consent" ignores whether the cl 11.3 conditions are met, and whether the consent is itself conditional or imposes new terms.

**Push back:**
- **Condition Precedent:** an unconditional written consent from Bluefen (or one subject only to conditions acceptable to the Buyer), on terms not materially less favourable to the Company, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied. The form must be satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably, and the CP is waivable only by the Buyer.
- Upgrade "reasonable endeavours" to "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours." Add Buyer participation rights in communications with Bluefen.
- Set a sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
- Consider an earn-out or deferred element tied to Bluefen retention, or a warranty that no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received.

### 13. Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 omitted from funds flow (DD-005)
**Why it matters:** These are Company liabilities triggered by the transaction. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Buyer would bear them after Completion. On-costs are not addressed either: payroll tax (NSW), superannuation guarantee, PAYG withholding and workers' compensation could add materially to the AUD 420,000.

**Push back:**
- Define them as **Transaction Costs/Debt-like items**, deducted from the price, including all on-costs and employer taxes.
- Pay them through Company payroll at Completion with correct withholding, funded by the Seller.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or related tax.
- Request the DD-005 documents to confirm the "continued employment" conditions. If bonuses vest after Completion, they should still be Seller-funded, for example through retention.

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals of AUD 330,000 (DD-008, DD-011)
**Facts:** Three "related" renewals of AUD 110,000 each, which the Seller itself says should be "read together for timing/scope." There is no statement of whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

**Why it matters:**
- Splitting into three equal tranches suggests structuring to stay under an approval threshold, for example an interim conduct of business consent threshold or an internal board limit. **Check the SPA interim covenant thresholds.**
- "Related" needs clarification: related to each other only, or is Sandbar a related party of Harbourglass? If the latter, this may be leakage or non-arm's length dealing.

**Push back:**
- Information request:
  - the relationship between Sandbar and the Seller group;
  - contract terms, term, termination rights and prepayment or accrual status;
  - business rationale.
- If entered or renewed in the run-up to sale without commercial need, require termination at Seller cost or treat the amounts as Debt/leakage.
- Add a warranty that all contracts with Seller-related parties are disclosed, on arm's length terms and terminable without cost. Include an anti-splitting provision in the conduct of business covenants (aggregate related transactions).

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
**Why it matters:** The Seller's own share register is not independent verification, and the Disclosure Letter itself says we have not verified it.

**Actions:**
- Our DD team should reconcile the register against ASIC records (company extract and historical extracts), the constitution, and any shareholder agreement, options, convertible notes, ESOP or issued rights.
- Run PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company.
- Completion deliverables: original share certificates (or a lost certificate indemnity), executed transfers, register updates and resignations.
- Add a warranty that there are no options, rights or Encumbrances over the shares. This should be Fundamental (item 1).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller's wording is carefully hedged ("does not describe it as a requirement for consent"; "does not state consent is required merely because shares are sold"). Neither statement says that consent is not required.

**Actions:**
- Our team should review the actual provisions. Leases and commercial contracts frequently deem a change of control to be an assignment.
- **Lease:** ensure the notification is given in time, as a Completion deliverable if pre-Completion notice is required.
- **Mossvale:** if any deeming language exists, add a consent CP or obtain a comfort letter.
- Add a warranty that no material contract is terminable or varied by reason of the Transaction, except as specifically disclosed.

---

## Part D: Funds flow
The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" but omits at least two items: the Riverlark payout and the DD-005 bonuses and on-costs. Require a revised funds flow showing:

- headline price of AUD 24m;
- less Debt (Riverlark payout, plus any other debt);
- less Transaction Costs (bonuses, on-costs, Seller adviser fees borne by the Company);
- plus or minus Cash and working capital adjustments;
- less any retention/escrow amounts;
- direct payments to creditors.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | "[STANDARD]" labels / efficiency note | Reject in writing. All positions remain open; confirm nothing was agreed |
| 1 | Fundamental warranties | 100% cap, 6–7 years, no thresholds |
| 2 | Limitations apply to all claims | Reverse default; carve out fraud, Fundamentals, tax, indemnities, leakage, covenants |
| 3 | Thresholds | Tipping basket about AUD 120k; de minimis AUD 10–15k with aggregation |
| 4 | General cap/period | 30% (or 20% with full ring-fencing); 24 months; tax 5–7 years |
| 5 | Tax/IP | Standalone tax indemnity; stronger IP warranties |
| 6 | General disclosure | Delete; fair and specific disclosure only; no updating |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Delete; pro-sandbagging clause (fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals) |
| 9 | Ironquay | CP: payment and confirmatory assignment; broad IP indemnity outside cap |
| 10 | DD-006 privacy incident | Urgent NDB status check; specific indemnity; retention; pre-Completion covenant |
| 11 | Riverlark | Payout at Completion from price; deed of release and PPSR releases as deliverables |
| 12 | Bluefen | Hard CP for unconditional consent satisfactory to Buyer; stronger endeavours; walk right |
| 13 | Bonuses of AUD 420k | Debt-like deduction including payroll tax, super and PAYG; specific indemnity |
| 14 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Clarify related-party status and splitting; Debt/leakage treatment or termination at Seller cost |
| 15 | Title | Independent ASIC/PPSR verification; Fundamental title warranty |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Review the actual clauses; notice/consent deliverables; no-change-of-control-trigger warranty |
| — | Funds flow | Revised funds flow itemising all deductions |
| — | Security for known risks | Escrow/retention for Ironquay, DD-006 and Bluefen, or consider W&I with specific indemnities sitting outside it |

## Priority next steps
1. **This week:** Send a holding response rejecting the [STANDARD] categorisation and the "agreed limitation package" premise.
2. **Urgent:** Send the DD-006 information request, because the Privacy Act timing may already be live.
3. Instruct the DD team on Ironquay payment verification, title searches, the lease and Mossvale clause review, and the Sandbar relationship.
4. Prepare a full Buyer mark-up of the SPA and Disclosure Letter reflecting the positions above.
5. Assess whether the volume of known risks justifies a price adjustment or retention in addition to the contractual protections.

**Caveat:** I have only the Seller's summary positions and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA or the underlying DD documents. The recommendations should be validated against the actual clause wording and the data room, and settled with NSW-qualified counsel on the deal.

**Push back:**

- Adopt a **fair disclosure standard**: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed with sufficient detail to allow a reasonable buyer to identify its nature and scope, and against the specific warranty it qualifies.
- Specific disclosures should qualify only the warranties they reference.
- **No updating:** the Disclosure Letter is fixed at signing. Any new matter arising between signing and Completion does not cure breach of repeated warranties. Instead it gives us a termination right or a claim.
- Data room cut-off: 22 September 2026 is six weeks ago. Confirm what has been added since, and that the index is frozen and agreed. Add a USB/archive copy deliverable.

### 7. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)
**Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Why it matters:** This is constructive knowledge, imputed through all our advisers. Combined with item 6, it amounts to near-total exclusion. It would also undermine the specific indemnities: the Seller could argue that because we knew about Ironquay, DD-006 and so on, we cannot claim.

**Push back:**
- Delete it. Our preferred position is an express pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not limit claims.
- **Fallback only:** limit it to the actual knowledge of named individuals of the Buyer (not advisers), of facts they knew constituted a breach, as at signing. Specific indemnities must be expressly excluded from its operation.

### 8. Disclosure Letter non-admission and reservation (1.4, 11)
These are broadly acceptable as boilerplate. We should add that the Disclosure Letter does not:
- extend or create a limitation;
- qualify a Fundamental Warranty, the tax indemnity or any specific indemnity.

## Part C: Specific transaction risks (known issues)

These are the substantive problems. Several the Seller itself discloses as unresolved, while simultaneously labelling the related clauses [STANDARD].

### 9. Ironquay IP (DD-004, DD-010; cl 11.1)
**Facts:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

**Why it matters:** Paperbark may not own IP that it is presumably using, and which may be core to the business. An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" covers only the AUD 180,000, not the real exposure: infringement claims, loss of the right to use, rework, injunctions or customer claims.

**Push back:**
- **Condition Precedent:**
  - evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, funded by the Seller or deducted from price; and
  - an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, including moral rights consents.
- Broaden the indemnity to all Losses from any defect in the Company's title to, or right to use, the SOW3 materials or any Ironquay deliverable. It should sit outside the general cap and thresholds, with a cap of at least 100% of price for core IP, or a separately negotiated figure.
- Ask the DD team to establish what SOW3 covers and how central it is to the product.

### 10. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
**Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records are potentially affected (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and notifiability were unknown as at 22 September and the investigation was "preliminary."

**Why it matters:**
- This is potentially an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme. The scheme requires a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within 30 days of the entity becoming aware of reasonable grounds to suspect a breach.
- By today, 5 November, that window may well have expired. If so, there is a risk of OAIC regulatory exposure under the enhanced penalty regime, plus customer notification and contractual consequences. A potential additional issue is that Bluefen or other customers' data may be involved.
- Calling it "not expected to be material" is an assertion with no supporting evidence.

**Push back / actions:**
- **Urgent information request:**
  - the date of awareness;
  - the status of the NDB assessment;
  - whether the OAIC or affected individuals have been notified;
  - whether the link was accessed (access logs) and whether it has been revoked;
  - any forensic report;
  - whose data is in the records, and whether any customer contract notification obligations have been triggered.
- **Pre-Completion covenant:** complete the investigation and any required notifications, with Buyer consultation rights.
- **Specific indemnity** covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party and customer claims. It should sit outside the cap and thresholds, and be unaffected by disclosure or knowledge.
- Consider a **retention/escrow** from the price until the matter is closed out or the limitation risk passes.
- Remove any characterisation of the matter as immaterial from the SPA.

### 11. Riverlark Bank facility (DD-003; cl 2 / 7)
**Facts:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The facility has a change of control clause (8.1) and a discharge clause (9.2). It has not been repaid and no discharge has been obtained.

**Why it matters:** A "release following Completion" is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis. Completion would likely trigger a change of control default under cl 8.1 while the security remains over Company assets that we will then own.

**Push back:**
- The full payout amount, including break costs, accrued interest and fees, is Debt deducted from the price and paid directly to Riverlark from the funds flow at Completion.
- **Completion deliverables:**
  - a payout letter;
  - an executed deed of release;
  - releases of all security interests (PPSR financing change statements), with any mortgage or real property discharges in registrable form.
- No post-Completion release. Add a Seller indemnity for any residual Riverlark liability.

### 12. Bluefen change of control consent (DD-002; cl 3 / 6.3)
**Facts:** Bluefen represents about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m FY26). Consent under cl 11.2 is subject to conditions in cl 11.3. There is no final consent and no evidence the conditions have been satisfied.

**Why it matters:** Losing Bluefen would materially impair the value we are paying AUD 24m for. "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation. Treating the CP as satisfied "on delivery of written consent" ignores whether the cl 11.3 conditions are met, and whether the consent is itself conditional or imposes new terms.

**Push back:**
- **Condition Precedent:** an unconditional written consent from Bluefen (or one subject only to conditions acceptable to the Buyer), on terms not materially less favourable to the Company, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied. The form must be satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably, and the CP is waivable only by the Buyer.
- Upgrade "reasonable endeavours" to "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours." Add Buyer participation rights in communications with Bluefen.
- Set a sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
- Consider an earn-out or deferred element tied to Bluefen retention, or a warranty that no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received.

### 13. Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 omitted from funds flow (DD-005)
**Why it matters:** These are Company liabilities triggered by the transaction. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Buyer would bear them after Completion. On-costs are not addressed either: payroll tax (NSW), superannuation guarantee, PAYG withholding and workers' compensation could add materially to the AUD 420,000.

**Push back:**
- Define them as **Transaction Costs/Debt-like items**, deducted from the price, including all on-costs and employer taxes.
- Pay them through Company payroll at Completion with correct withholding, funded by the Seller.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or related tax.
- Request the DD-005 documents to confirm the "continued employment" conditions. If bonuses vest after Completion, they should still be Seller-funded, for example through retention.

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals of AUD 330,000 (DD-008, DD-011)
**Facts:** Three "related" renewals of AUD 110,000 each, which the Seller itself says should be "read together for timing/scope." There is no statement of whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

**Why it matters:**
- Splitting into three equal tranches suggests structuring to stay under an approval threshold, for example an interim conduct of business consent threshold or an internal board limit. **Check the SPA interim covenant thresholds.**
- "Related" needs clarification: related to each other only, or is Sandbar a related party of Harbourglass? If the latter, this may be leakage or non-arm's length dealing.

**Push back:**
- Information request:
  - the relationship between Sandbar and the Seller group;
  - contract terms, term, termination rights and prepayment or accrual status;
  - business rationale.
- If entered or renewed in the run-up to sale without commercial need, require termination at Seller cost or treat the amounts as Debt/leakage.
- Add a warranty that all contracts with Seller-related parties are disclosed, on arm's length terms and terminable without cost. Include an anti-splitting provision in the conduct of business covenants (aggregate related transactions).

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
**Why it matters:** The Seller's own share register is not independent verification, and the Disclosure Letter itself says we have not verified it.

**Actions:**
- Our DD team should reconcile the register against ASIC records (company extract and historical extracts), the constitution, and any shareholder agreement, options, convertible notes, ESOP or issued rights.
- Run PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company.
- Completion deliverables: original share certificates (or a lost certificate indemnity), executed transfers, register updates and resignations.
- Add a warranty that there are no options, rights or Encumbrances over the shares. This should be Fundamental (item 1).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller's wording is carefully hedged ("does not describe it as a requirement for consent"; "does not state consent is required merely because shares are sold"). Neither statement says that consent is not required.

**Actions:**
- Our team should review the actual provisions. Leases and commercial contracts frequently deem a change of control to be an assignment.
- **Lease:** ensure the notification is given in time, as a Completion deliverable if pre-Completion notice is required.
- **Mossvale:** if any deeming language exists, add a consent CP or obtain a comfort letter.
- Add a warranty that no material contract is terminable or varied by reason of the Transaction, except as specifically disclosed.

## Part D: Funds flow
The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" but omits at least two items: the Riverlark payout and the DD-005 bonuses and on-costs. Require a revised funds flow showing:

- headline price of AUD 24m;
- less Debt (Riverlark payout, plus any other debt);
